churches.assessment: Abilene BIC is one of three BIC congregations in this small Kansas town that anchors the BIC presence in the Midwest. Pastor Matt leads. The church website provides only a first-name reference, which is common practice in some Anabaptist congregations but limits external verification. The Brethren in Christ tradition combines Anabaptist (Mennonite-rooted) believer's baptism and peace witness with Pietist personal-holiness emphasis and Wesleyan sanctification. Yellow rating reflects the BIC denomination's women-in-ministry allowance and the limited public information about the local pastor's teaching specifics. For a man in Abilene seeking a smaller Anabaptist congregation, visit and ask about local elder polity.

churches.assessment: All Saints Church in New Holland, PA (Lancaster County) was established in 1999 as a church plant of Christ Church (Moscow, ID) and is a member of the CREC. Dr. Gregg Strawbridge served faithfully as pastor for twenty years (2002–2022) and is the founder of the Strawbridge Ministerial Forum hosted by the church. Following his passing in 2022, Rev. Kasey Horvath (lead) and Rev. Brandon Gilanyi (associate) were installed in 2023, and the congregation relocated to a historic building in New Holland in 2024. Theologically this is a classic Moscow-network CREC congregation: Reformed, covenant-renewal liturgical worship, paedocommunion, classical Christian education ethos, patriarchal household vision, and postmillennial cultural engagement. The one area calling for direct inquiry is soteriology — CREC churches have historically been associated with Federal Vision theology, which modifies traditional Reformed articulations of justification. Ask the elders directly about their position on FV and justification. For a Reformed man in Lancaster County seeking a serious, liturgical, Moscow-aligned CREC home, this is the obvious first visit.

churches.assessment: Apostles Anglican Church in west Knoxville is an ACNA parish in the Anglican Diocese of the South, led by Rector Rev. Jack King — who also serves as Dean of the Tennessee Convocation (ADOTS). He has been rector for over 13 years, providing mature pastoral leadership. The church is known for its 'scruffy hospitality' ethos and has been profiled in ACNA communications. The parish maintains one of the richest liturgical rhythms profiled here: Sunday services at 8:45 AM (with choral music), 11:15 AM (with acoustic music), plus 10:10 Formation Hour; Monday-Thursday daily Morning Prayer (8:30 AM), Midday Prayer (noon), and Evening Prayer (4:00 PM); and a Wednesday Noon Eucharist with Healing Service. Three strategic priorities include becoming a mother church, deepening spiritual formation across all ages, and serving the local neighborhood. ACNA 39 Articles framework with male-only ordination. Strong green-rated Anglican option for the Knoxville metro.

churches.assessment: Bethany Grace Fellowship in East Earl, Pennsylvania is one of the founding congregations of the Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) — the conservative Anabaptist-evangelical body that broke from the Mennonite Church USA merger in 2002 over doctrinal and sexuality concerns. Founded in 1957 as Blue Ball Mennonite Church, renamed Bethany Mennonite, and now Bethany Grace Fellowship, the congregation is led by Lead Pastor Steve Benedict. AMEC's two-fold confessional commitment — to evangelical orthodoxy and to historic biblical Anabaptism — gives this church the theological clarity that newer MC USA progressive drift lacks. For a Lancaster County man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist congregation with explicit orthodoxy commitments and full ministry portfolio, Bethany Grace Fellowship is a strong candidate.

score_notes.scripture: Bethel elevates 'fresh revelation', prophetic words, and impartation to practical co-authority with Scripture.

score_notes.soteriology: Prosperity-adjacent 'atmosphere of heaven' theology; signs-and-wonders emphasis overshadows substitutionary atonement in practice.
score_notes.cultural: Charismatic celebrity culture; Jesus Culture / Bethel Music global export; NAR apostolic-prophetic networking.
score_notes.denominational: Independent; central node of the New Apostolic Reformation. No external confessional accountability.

score_notes.mission: 'Worldwide transformation through revival' and 'manifest presence' — mission diluted by signs-and-wonders emphasis.

churches.assessment: Bethel Church Redding is a controversial charismatic congregation led by Bill Johnson. The NAR (New Apostolic Reformation) connections are concerning. Exercise significant theological caution.

Church records trace roots to 1790 and include the legacy of Nannie Bland David, missionary to Africa (1880-1885) — the kind of Great Commission heritage that should be honored. Today the congregation is a BGAV member under Rev. George Brown's leadership. The standard BGAV concerns apply: no inerrancy requirement, women in ministry permitted, moderate denominational framework. Rev. Brown's theological convictions are unknown. Bethlehem's deep Baptist mission heritage makes it worth a visit — if the current congregation has maintained evangelical convictions within the BGAV framework, it could be a valuable kingdom partner for USMC Ministries. Contact directly to assess current doctrinal health.

churches.assessment: Blue Ridge Grace Brethren Church has a remarkable 100-year history in Winchester, Virginia — founded in 1925 as the First Brethren Church of Winchester after a pioneering group of believers sold homemade cruellers to fund construction. This is the kind of sacrificial church-building story that marks a serious congregation. The Fellowship of Grace Brethren Churches provides accountability within a conservative evangelical, dispensationally informed tradition. Bible teaching is central to Grace Brethren DNA, with a doctrinal affirmation of Scripture's inerrancy and final authority. The Winchester Shenandoah Valley context gives this church a community role stretching back a century. For a man in Winchester or Frederick County wanting a smaller, doctrinally stable evangelical church with deep local roots, Blue Ridge Grace Brethren is worth visiting.

Backus holds a Ph.D. — unusually strong academic credentials for a small-denomination pastor. The BPC was formed in 1937 by Carl McIntire, J. Oliver Buswell, and Allan MacRae as a conservative fundamentalist-leaning breakaway Presbyterian denomination holding the Westminster Standards with a pronounced emphasis on biblical inerrancy and separation from liberalism. The denomination is very small (only 28 churches across the US and one in Canada) — MOOP readers considering BPC congregations should understand they will likely find a small, tight-knit, strongly-convictional Reformed fellowship rather than a large-church experience. churches.assessment: Bridge Church Fredericksburg has one of the cleanest statements of faith among the churches surveyed: Trinitarian, Bible as final authority, salvation by grace through faith, baptism as response (not requirement), Great Commission-focused. The church was launched in 2019 by Max Lucado and the Oak Hills Church (San Antonio) team — Jimmy Pruitt was the former campus pastor who was invited by Max to take it independent. That's a vote of confidence from one of the most respected evangelical communicators of our generation. The two-service Sunday model with sermon notes and discipleship resources indicates a substantive ministry rather than a casual social gathering. Main watch items: no explicit complementarian statement, no formal denominational accountability, no confirmed men's ministry. The 'inter-denominational' description means Moop would need to probe the gender/leadership question directly before committing. Overall one of the more theologically promising independent churches in the FXBG area.

churches.assessment: Butter Valley Community Church in Bally, Pennsylvania — formerly known as Hereford Mennonite Church — was the leading congregation that organized the Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) in 2001-2002 when conservative Anabaptists departed Mennonite Church USA over doctrinal and sexuality concerns. AMEC's two-fold confessional commitment to evangelical orthodoxy and historic biblical Anabaptism gives this congregation rare theological clarity for a Mennonite-rooted body. For a Berks County or Boyertown-area man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist congregation with explicit orthodoxy heritage, Butter Valley is one of the strongest options in southeastern Pennsylvania.

Affiliated with the Beachy Amish-Mennonite Fellowship, the church practices plain Anabaptist witness with bishop/minister/deacon polity, male-only ordination, plain dress, women's head covering, and a simple agricultural lifestyle. The congregation also operates Calvary Fellowship Mennonite School. Pastor Sam Troyer leads per 2023-2024 records. The Beachy tradition arose from a 1927 division in the Casselman River Old Order Amish in Pennsylvania, led by Bishop Moses M. Beachy — adopting evangelical outreach while maintaining plain Anabaptist conviction. Green rating.

Located at 206 Pine Valley Rd and serving Marines and families from Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River, this church offers a stable, confessional alternative in a region dominated by Baptist and Methodist congregations. The pastor name is not displayed on the staff page (a link to "Meet Our Pastor" exists but content was not directly verifiable on fetch), so verify pastor on visit. Men's ministry is not visibly advertised — Lutheran congregations often run men's formation through Bible classes and Lutheran Hour Ministries rather than branded "men's ministry" — but worth asking on a visit. Strong recommendation for confessional Lutheran or liturgically-minded Christians in the Onslow County area.

Henry Clay was a founding pewholder when the parish was organized August 25, 1808; he funded a family pew though he did not formally join until 1847 at age 70 (baptized by Rev. Berkley at Ashland on June 22, 1847 because the church was under construction; confirmed by Bishop Benjamin Bosworth Smith at Transylvania's Morrison Hall on July 18, 1847). Now the cathedral of the Episcopal Diocese of Lexington under Dean Carol Wade. RED per TEC rubric.

churches.assessment: Christ Church Waco is an ACNA parish in the Diocese of Fort Worth, led by Priest-in-Charge Fr. Jeff Logan, who arrived in October 2025 after 22 years as a Navy chaplain. His academic credentials are unusually strong: B.A. from DePauw, M.Div. from the Episcopal Theological Seminary of the Southwest, and D.Min. from Fuller Theological Seminary. The parish maintains a full liturgical rhythm: Sunday 8:00 AM and 10:45 AM Holy Eucharist with 9:30 AM Catechesis, plus a Wednesday Noon Eucharist. Supported by Fr. Andrew Hollinger (Diocesan Curate, M.Div. Nashotah House 2024) and Rev. Thomas Hunter (Deacon, ordained 2024). Self-describes as 'a church of the great commandment, the great commission, and the Great Tradition.' ACNA 39 Articles framework aligns with MOOP's rubric. Strong green-rated Anglican option for Central Texas.

churches.assessment: Christ Kirk DC is a confessional Reformed, evangelical church in Washington, DC affiliated with the Christ Church Moscow tradition (Doug Wilson, author and theologian). The church affirms the Apostles' Creed, Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition, and Westminster Confession of Faith — a strong confessional foundation. Preaching from Pastor Garrett Craw is expository, Word-centered, and theologically serious. Strengths: genuine commitment to Reformation doctrine, strong complementarianism, serious men's discipleship, winsome confessional faith in an antagonistic cultural context. Caution: the Doug Wilson association brings controversy — Wilson's provocative cultural commentary and church planting theology attract both admirers and fierce critics; men should evaluate this association thoughtfully. The church has been targeted by progressive activist groups, which speaks to both its clear doctrinal stance and its cultural visibility. For a man wanting serious Reformed theology and strong masculine leadership culture in DC, Christ Kirk is worth serious consideration.

churches.assessment: Christ Methodist Church of Auburn is a post-2022 Global Methodist plant, having voted to join the GMC and called Dr. Tony McCullough as their first senior minister in 2023. Nearly 700 members stood together at their first membership vows ceremony. The congregation currently gathers at the Greystone Office and Ministry Center while actively exploring permanent building options. As a GMC church, they affirm orthodox Wesleyan theology, traditional marriage, and the historic Christian faith — the specific reasons the GMC separated from the progressive UMC. Male lead pastor, active men's Bible study, and children's ministry make this a strong Methodist option for the Auburn area. The one caution flag is that the GMC's Alabama-Florida-West Georgia Conference ordination stance on women as elders should be verified; GMC varies by conference. Overall a green-eligible, solidly orthodox Wesleyan church worth further on-the-ground review.

Chelsea holds the same top pastoral title as Judah and preaches Sunday services. Church Clarity scores Churchome "Clear: Egalitarian" on women in leadership. Per MOOP rubric (female pastor at senior level → RED), this is a hard RED on gender and leadership. Additional concerns: (1) LGBTQ policy is publicly Undisclosed — Chelsea Smith answered the gay-pastor question with rhetorical inclusion rather than a policy answer; (2) T.D. Jakes — historically associated with Oneness/modalist Christology — joined the Churchome board around 2021, raising Trinity-adjacency concerns even though Churchome itself is formally Trinitarian; (3) the celebrity-pastor culture (Justin Bieber and other A-list members) and Churchome app-driven model represent a particular branch of attractional evangelicalism that prioritizes accessibility over doctrinal precision. The Belltown Seattle campus at 2700 1st Ave is the flagship location. Judah Smith is a gifted communicator; the preaching is grace-focused, narrative, and culturally engaged. But the egalitarian leadership structure, LGBTQ ambiguity, and board composition make this RED per MOOP convictions. This is NOT Mars Hill (which dissolved 2014 under Mark Driscoll); Churchome is a different church with a different doctrinal posture. Adam visited Churchome in Seattle.

churches.assessment: Common Ground Church has a compelling origin story: 21 years as a mobile congregation finally receiving a permanent home — the historic First Christian Church building on Washington Ave, gifted free of charge by a 100-year-old congregation choosing to bless its successor. That kind of kingdom generosity, and CG's decision to then give their former meeting house (The Old Silk Mill space) to a Filipino congregation, shows genuine missional health. Lead Pastor Gregg Jennings trained at Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (among the most rigorous conservative evangelical seminaries), studied both Theology and Global Missions, and has pastored CG since 2009. The church has elders, active ministries including a men's night, kids, and youth programs. Main yellow flags: Melissa Southall holds a staff pastoral title and was ordained in 2021 (female ordained pastor in a worship/outreach role); the inclusive table language may reflect a broad-welcome posture or a softer ecclesiology — worth hearing a sermon and asking Gregg directly about his complementarian convictions and Scripture inerrancy. Overall a promising, established community church worth visiting.

score_notes.christology: OPC subscribes to the Westminster Standards — orthodox Trinitarian Christology, Chalcedonian two-natures, virgin birth, bodily resurrection.
score_notes.scripture: Westminster Confession ch. 1 affirms plenary verbal inspiration and inerrancy of the Scriptures as the only rule of faith and life.

score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: Community Presbyterian Church (OPC) is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel is an Apostolic/Oneness Pentecostal church — and that's a hard stop for theological alignment. Oneness Pentecostalism denies the eternal distinction of the three persons of the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), teaching instead that 'Jesus' is the only name of God and the three are merely different modes. This places it outside the bounds of Nicene orthodoxy — the same line historic Christianity drew in 325 AD. Additionally, most Apostolic churches teach that speaking in tongues and baptism in 'Jesus' name only' are necessary for salvation, adding works to justification. The congregation may be sincere and passionate, but the core theological framework disqualifies it for anyone committed to trinitarian Christianity and faith-alone soteriology. Not recommended.

churches.assessment: Covenant Bible Church is a Reformed Baptist congregation in North Georgetown (Austin metro area) planted and led by pastor-theologian Joel Webbon. The church affirms the 1689 Second London Baptist Confession — one of the most rigorous and historically grounded confessions in Protestant Christianity — placing it firmly within the Reformed, biblical-patriarchy, and expository preaching tradition. Webbon is a nationally known voice through Right Response Ministries, openly advocating biblical patriarchy (he explicitly rejects the 'complementarian' label) and Christian Nationalism. He has headlined panels on biblical patriarchy alongside Doug Wilson, Eric Conn, and Dale Partridge, and the church is networked with Church & Family Life (Scott Brown). He has generated controversy for some of his political/cultural commentary — men should evaluate this directly rather than through secondhand coverage. The church's theological foundation is solid: Trinitarian, faith-alone soteriology, male eldership, expository preaching, and Great Commission focus. The one caution is independence — no formal denominational structure means accountability rests on the internal elder structure. For men in the Georgetown/Austin area seeking a doctrinally serious, unapologetically patriarchal church, this is worth a visit. Personal note: Connected to Joel Webb (Webbon) referenced in USMC Ministries network.

churches.assessment: Covenant Life Church has an extraordinary and complicated history. Founded in 1977 by C.J. Mahaney as a charismatic fellowship, it evolved into one of America's most theologically sophisticated Reformed evangelical churches — hosting conferences, producing discipleship resources, and nurturing a generation of serious Bible-saturated Christians. But CLC also became ground zero for significant controversies: the Sovereign Grace Churches abuse lawsuit (2012), C.J. Mahaney's leadership scandals, and most publicly — Joshua Harris (pastor 2004-2015) publicly deconstructing his faith in 2019 and renouncing Christianity. Current pastor Mark Mitchell leads a congregation that has weathered enormous institutional trauma. The theological framework (Reformed, complementarian, Gospel-centered) remains intact on paper. The questions are about institutional health, pastoral culture, and whether the congregation has genuinely processed and healed from years of controversy. Worth visiting with eyes wide open.

churches.assessment: Covenant Presbyterian Church Harrisonburg is a PCA congregation under the Blue Ridge Presbytery — arguably the gold standard for Reformed evangelical accountability in American denominational life. The Westminster Confession of Faith provides the most rigorous doctrinal framework of any evangelical denomination. Rev. Todd Pruitt is a known Reformed voice who brings theological seriousness to pastoral ministry. Two full morning services (8:30 AM and 11:15 AM) signal a congregation of meaningful size with the infrastructure to support solid men's, children's, and discipleship ministries. The James Madison University context (Harrisonburg is a college town) gives Covenant opportunities for campus ministry and young adult outreach alongside its established membership. For a man in Harrisonburg or the Shenandoah Valley wanting the strongest Reformed confessional accountability available, Covenant Presbyterian is the benchmark.

churches.assessment: East Whittier Friends Church is the lifelong home meeting of Richard Milhous Nixon — the 37th President was raised here from age 9, played piano in Sunday school, taught Sunday school as a young attorney, and remained a member until his death in 1994. The congregation is part of Friends Southwest, the evangelical/programmed branch of Quakerism — distinct from the liberal unprogrammed Friends General Conference (FGC) and Friends United Meeting (FUM) which have moved toward LGBT affirmation. Evangelical Friends affirm Trinitarian orthodoxy, biblical authority, and grace-through-faith soteriology in the Richmond Declaration tradition. Worship is bilingual (English/Spanish) and programmed — looking more like a contemporary evangelical service than the silent meetings stereotypically associated with Quakers. Female pastoral leadership is present (Pastora Delia Madrid) — consistent with Quakerism's 17th-century affirmation of women in ministry, but yellow on MOOP's rubric. Solid green at the denominational and theological core; historic Americana.

churches.assessment: Eastside Baptist Church in Twin Falls, Idaho is a 1689 Confessional Reformed Baptist church with a plurality of elders, age-integrated worship, and a robust confessional foundation. Founded in 1972, this church holds to the full 1689 London Baptist Confession including the appendix on baptism. The elder-led structure (Thompson, Martinez) with deacons reflects biblical governance. Their adoption of resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription demonstrates a church willing to take stands on cultural issues from Scripture — not hiding behind neutrality. Men's Book Study and age-integrated model mean men are formed as household leaders, not shuffled into a separate program. Four services per week (Sunday AM, Sunday PM, Sunday School, Wednesday evening) indicates a serious, committed congregation. This is an all-GREEN church — rare and worthy of attention for any Reformed Baptist in the Pacific Northwest.

Charlotte is a thin EFCA metro in the directory, and this is one of the historic anchor congregations for EFCA in NC.

churches.pastor_credentials: BA Elizabethtown College, MS South University, MA Liberty University, EdD Eastern University

score_notes.christology: Trinitarian orthodoxy. Affirms Apostles' Creed. Christ alone for salvation.
score_notes.scripture: Bible as final authority. Adheres to BFC 28 Articles of Faith. High view of Scripture.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Elder Alex Kocman leads men's discipleship groups at the church. Confirmed by personal relationship with user — Kocman, who writes publicly at American Reformer and Founders Ministries on biblical manhood, carries that conviction into hands-on men's formation inside the local body. Update 2026-09-25: he has publicly said he is preparing to transition to Citylight Church Dover. This note describes his role at Faith until that move is complete.
score_notes.soteriology: Doctrines of grace (TULIP). Salvation by grace through faith alone. Reformed soteriology.
score_notes.gender: Patriarchal household vision, male headship, anti-feminist. Church mission statement is explicitly household-focused: 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household.' Male-only elders and pastors per BFC bylaws. Elder Alex Kocman is a published voice at American Reformer and Founders Ministries on biblical manhood, male headship, and the missions-critical nature of complementarian/patriarchal order. The church holds a complementarian label but with appropriate biblical-patriarchy guardrails — the hard line on male-only elder rule, an unapologetic household-by-household mission, and Kocman's public writing against the cultural crisis of masculinity — that prevent the usual drift of soft complementarianism into functional egalitarianism. Caveat: church retains a female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill); by BFC polity deacons 'do not exercise rule or spiritual authority,' so this is a serving role rather than an office of authority.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led with 3 elders (Senior Pastor + 2). Deacon board for material needs. Denominational accountability through BFC.
score_notes.preaching: Expository, sermon-based teaching through Scripture. Reformed tradition. Podcast sermons available.
score_notes.mission: Church planting emphasis. Elder Alex Kocman directs communications for ABWE (international missions). Bold witness central. Update 2026-09-25: he has publicly said he is staying at ABWE while preparing to serve more closely with Citylight Church Dover.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT language. Conservative Reformed stance. Family-focused mission statement.
score_notes.denominational: Bible Fellowship Church denomination. Accountable to BFC conference. Self-governing under elder board.

churches.gender_detail: Patriarchal household vision, male headship, anti-feminist. Male-only elders (Wesley Bunting, Alex Kocman, Joshua Vann). Female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill) on board — non-authority role per BFC polity.
churches.assessment: Faith Bible Fellowship Church of York is a Reformed, evangelical, baptistic church in the BFC denomination. Pastor Wesley Bunting leads a solid elder-governed congregation committed to the doctrines of grace and expository preaching. The church's mission — 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household' — reflects a patriarchal, family-centered, Great Commission focus. Elder Alex Kocman's role with ABWE, his published work at American Reformer and Founders Ministries, and his hands-on men's discipleship leadership give the church unusually strong DNA on biblical manhood, male headship, and international missions. The one polity detail worth asking about directly: the church retains a female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill) under BFC's rule that deacons 'do not exercise rule or spiritual authority' — elder rule remains entirely male. Doctrinally and practically, green across the board. Worth visiting. Update 2026-09-25: Elder Alex Kocman has publicly said he and his family are preparing to transition over the coming months to Citylight Church Dover, where he will help lead worship and grow in pastoral ministry. He is staying at ABWE. The elders at Faith are supporting the move. It is not a departure over conflict. Pastor Wesley Bunting remains the shepherd accountable for this church.

churches.assessment: Fellowship Missionary Baptist Church Chicago — known affectionately as "the Ship" — was founded September 10, 1950 by Rev. Dr. Clay Evans (1925-2019), the gospel-and-civil-rights legend whose ministry launched the careers of more than 90 ministers, including Rev. Jesse Louis Jackson Sr., who was ordained at Fellowship in 1968. Evans opened the church's doors to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. during the Chicago Freedom Movement and helped Jackson launch Operation Breadbasket and later Operation PUSH/Rainbow Coalition from this congregation. Evans served as founding National Board Chairman of Rainbow PUSH 1971-1976. Rev. Charles Jenkins succeeded Evans as Senior Pastor after Evans's December 8, 2000 retirement. Listed for civic/political/civil-rights historical significance.

churches.assessment: First African Baptist Church of Richmond is one of the most historically significant Black churches in the United States — founded in 1841 from the Black members of Richmond's First Baptist Church, at a time when both enslaved and free Black Christians gathered to worship. The church has been a spiritual anchor in Richmond's Black community through slavery, Reconstruction, Jim Crow, and the Civil Rights movement. Dr. Rodney D. Waller is the 10th Senior Pastor, serving for 16+ years and described as an 'anointed' preacher with deep community roots. The theological concerns are the standard ones for NBC/BGAV churches: no formal inerrancy requirement, women in ministry permitted, and the ever-present tension in historically Black mainline churches between prophetic social justice and Gospel proclamation. USMC Ministries should approach with respect for the extraordinary historical legacy while verifying current doctrinal commitments. This church is a kingdom partner candidate for outreach even if full theological alignment is uncertain.

churches.assessment: First Baptist Hammond is one of the most controversial churches in American Christianity. Founded 1887, it became a megachurch under Jack Hyles. The church has been plagued by scandals: Jack Schaap (Hyles' successor and son-in-law) was convicted of transporting a minor across state lines for sexual activity (2012). Multiple staff/associated pastors have faced similar charges. The institutional culture has been widely criticized for prioritizing numbers, easy-believism, and personality-driven leadership over genuine accountability. Current pastor John Wilkerson has attempted to restore credibility, but the institutional DNA remains a major concern. NOT recommended without extensive personal investigation.

churches.assessment: First Baptist Church Newport News has a remarkable 140-year history on the Virginia Peninsula, organized in 1881 and formally constituted in 1883. Dr. Randy Shepley III leads this historic congregation. The concern is the BGAV affiliation — the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Baptist body in Virginia, distinct from the more conservative SBC of Virginia. BGAV is connected with the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship and takes a theologically moderate stance that allows greater diversity on Scripture, gender roles, and cultural issues than the SBC's Baptist Faith & Message 2000. This doesn't make FBCNN a bad church — but it means verification is required. Visit, listen to the preaching, ask directly about their stance on Scripture's authority and complementarian convictions before committing. The historic pedigree is impressive; the denominational framework is less clearly conservative.

Per refined SBC threshold (BFM2000 + men's ministry), prior enrichment confirms SBC Cooperative Program giving and 'Fearlessly Following Jesus' men's ministry — this would qualify for green EXCEPT that women holding 'Minister' titles (Megan Langan as 'Minister for Single Adults; Pastoral Care & Women's Ministry'; Tera Kouba as 'Minister of International/Asian Ministries') is a substantive yellow — not a red flag (no female senior pastor, no affirming language) but exceeds standard SBC complementarian practice. churches.assessment: First Baptist San Antonio is a historic downtown SBC church (est. ~1861) led by Senior Pastor Chris Johnson. Doctrinally strong: affirms Jesus as co-equal with the Father, Scripture as God's Word and 'supreme and final source of truth,' and salvation as God's free gift through personal faith in Christ. Notable strength: dedicated men's ministry ('Fearlessly Following Jesus') and a unique Bible study integration model where the same passage is studied across all ministries. The church broadcasts on KSAT-12 television, suggesting substantive preaching. One concern: women hold 'Minister' titles (Megan Langan, Tera Kouba), which goes beyond traditional complementarian support roles while stopping short of 'Pastor' titles. The senior pastoral role remains male. Extensive ministry portfolio including Spanish and Asian/international outreach. Worth deeper evaluation — one of the stronger SBC churches in the directory with solid doctrine and intentional discipleship.

The congregation was organized in 1903; the original sanctuary stood at 6th & Avenue E and the present church is at 401 E Cypress. Listed here for civic/political historical significance.

churches.assessment: First Methodist Church of Waco is a historic 1859 congregation that was among the earliest to leave the UMC and join the Global Methodist Church in 2022. Rev. Dr. Mike Voigts became Senior Pastor in May 2025 after serving as a professor at Asbury Theological Seminary — bringing academic Wesleyan depth to the pulpit. The church operates three campuses: the Main Campus on Cobbs Drive, the Speegleville Campus, and a Baylor Campus specifically reaching university students with a Tuesday 7 PM service. One flag worth noting: Rev. Dr. Blossom Matthews serves as Senior Associate Pastor, meaning this particular GMC church does appoint women to pastoral roles (distinct from formal elder ordination, which varies by conference). This places the church closer to the YELLOW end of the gender-rubric for readers committed to male-only ordination. For those comfortable with women in teaching/associate roles but male senior leadership, it's a solid orthodox Wesleyan option in Central Texas.

churches.assessment: First Presbyterian Church of Orlando is a 135+ year historic congregation that voted to join the Evangelical Presbyterian Church (EPC) in 2012, departing the progressive PCUSA. Rev. Dr. David D. Swanson (M.Div., Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary) has served as Senior Pastor for over 20 years. churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Baptist Church is one of the older Baptist congregations in the city, located on historic Princess Anne Street. The mission language is straightforwardly Christ-centered — 'on mission together, striving to continue the work of Christ' with commitments to 'the praise of God and the proclamation of the word of God' and 'the preservation, instruction, and spreading of the Gospel.' That's a healthy public-facing posture. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream, separate from SBC, and the denominational structure allows women in pastoral roles and leans progressive on several fronts. Pastor David Haun's theological convictions are unknown. Before visiting, Moop should confirm the church's stance on Scripture inerrancy, women in ministry, and elder accountability. The Princess Anne address is prime downtown Fredericksburg — a historic congregation worth investigating. (Also operates as "FXBG Baptist Church" with shorter URL/branding via fxbgbaptist.org.)

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Church of Christ has a lot going for it: high Scripture authority, Trinitarian orthodoxy, complementarian leadership with male elder plurality, expository DNA, and no cultural drift indicators. The congregation explicitly states they are 'not a denomination, but simply Christians that belong to the body of believers of which Christ is the head' — that's a healthy posture. The hard stop for a faith-alone evangelical like Moop: Churches of Christ traditionally teach that baptism is necessary for salvation, not merely a sign of it. This is the theological fault line that separates the Restoration Movement from mainstream evangelicalism — and it's a real one. Not a cult, not heresy in the broad sense, but incompatible with sola fide. Worth a conversation with leadership to clarify their exact position on baptism and salvation before getting deeper. Some congregations in this tradition have moved toward a more grace-emphasis soteriology; some have not.

churches.assessment: Grace Church Lynchburg is an Evangelical Free Church of America congregation with 35+ years of faithful ministry in the Lynchburg/Madison Heights corridor. Founded in 1988, Grace Church has served through six rented facilities and is now building a permanent home across from its current meeting place at Monelison Middle School — a sign of a congregation committed to long-term community investment. The EFCA is one of the strongest evangelical networks for theological accountability: clear confessional statement on inerrancy, male-only senior pastors, Great Commission mission, and strong doctrinal formation. For a man in the Madison Heights/Lynchburg area wanting a smaller, community-embedded church with solid evangelical credentials, Grace Church EFCA is worth visiting.

churches.assessment: Grace Community Church in Chesapeake is a small-to-medium non-denominational congregation led by Pastor Stephen Hildebrandt. The church distinguishes itself in Hampton Roads by its commitment to expository teaching — chapter by chapter, verse by verse, precept upon precept. This is one of the strongest indicators of a healthy teaching church. The home fellowship model (Sunday afternoon gatherings in homes throughout Chesapeake) reflects a shepherding culture that goes beyond Sunday-only programming. Hildebrandt's personal testimony — an aerospace engineer who came to Christ and found his calling in ministry — suggests depth and earnest faith. Key unknowns: formal statement of faith, elder gender policy, and church accountability structure. For men in Chesapeake who want a teaching church with real community, GCC deserves serious investigation. The expository approach and home fellowship culture set it apart from most Hampton Roads options.

churches.assessment: Grace Episcopal Church is the historic home parish of President Gerald R. Ford and Betty Ford, who were married in the old sanctuary in 1948 and whose private funeral was held here in 2006. The parish remains beautiful and historic, with strong choral and liturgical traditions in the Episcopal style. However, for the MOOP rubric, Grace is firmly within The Episcopal Church (TEC) — a denomination that since 1976 has ordained women to all orders, since 2003 has consecrated openly gay bishops, and since 2015 has authorized same-sex marriage rites. These denominational positions place Grace at red on cultural, gender, and denominational dimensions of the rubric. The parish is in a season of transition following the 2024 dissolution-by-merger of the Episcopal Diocese of Western Michigan into the new Diocese of the Great Lakes. Beautiful history. Significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.

churches.assessment: Grace Reformed Church is a historic Washington DC congregation with a fascinating history — it was the church of President Theodore Roosevelt during his time in the White House. Originally an Evangelical and Reformed Church congregation, it merged into the United Church of Christ (UCC) in 1957. Today the UCC is one of the most theologically liberal denominations in America, fully affirming LGBTQ+ clergy and same-sex marriage, rejecting biblical inerrancy, and embracing pluralistic soteriology. Individual UCC congregations vary in their degree of liberalism, but the denomination provides no orthodox accountability. The historic building and Roosevelt connection make it interesting from a historical standpoint, but for a man seeking biblically sound Word ministry and gospel-centered community, Grace Reformed DC is not recommended. Seek out Reformed churches in the area that have maintained confessional integrity.

churches.gender_detail: Pastor David D. Flowers (male) — Senior Pastor since 2016
churches.assessment: Grantham Church is the historic flagship of the Brethren in Christ U.S. denomination, founded near the campus of what is now Messiah University in Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania. Pastor David Flowers brings a serious academic-pastoral pedigree — biblical studies graduate degrees, 25+ years across Texas, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, and a published trajectory in New Testament studies and early Christian ethics. The Brethren in Christ tradition holds together Anabaptist peace witness with Wesleyan-Holiness soteriology and pietist devotion — a hybrid that produces mission-minded, Bible-loving congregations but with synergistic rather than Reformed soteriology. For a Mechanicsburg-area man wanting a Christ-centered, mission-oriented church with a graduate-degreed expositor in the pulpit, Grantham deserves a careful look. The denominational yellow flag is gender — BIC USA does permit women's ordination at congregational discretion, though Grantham's senior pastoral office is male.

churches.assessment: Greater Tabernacle Missionary Baptist (Lawrenceburg TN) called Rev. Shonda Reynolds Christian as senior pastor in June 2015 and was disfellowshipped by the Lawrence County Association of Baptists by a 73-4 vote on October 12, 2015 — the association explicitly citing the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 Article VI ('the office of pastor is limited to men as qualified by Scripture'). Pastor Christian, who continues to lead the church a decade later, publicly characterized the disfellowship as 'unchristian' and challenged the binding force of the 2000 BF&M revision. This case set the early modern precedent for SBC state-association action against churches with female senior pastors and remains the longest-running Mid-South case.

churches.assessment: Harrisburg Brethren in Christ Church is a city-center congregation under Pastor Hank Johnson, who came up through this very church — first as Youth Pastor (2008), then Pastor of Discipleship & Youth (2013), and finally Senior Pastor (November 2018). His backstory is striking: born in Monrovia, Liberia, he and his family lived as immigrants and refugees through Sierra Leone and Côte d'Ivoire before settling in Palisades Park, NJ and Philadelphia. His MDiv and his work on the BIC Historical Society board and as Atlantic Conference assistant moderator suggest a serious denominational pastor. For a Harrisburg-area man wanting a Bible-rooted, urban, mission-oriented church under male senior leadership in the Anabaptist-Holiness tradition, Harrisburg BIC merits a careful visit. Denominational yellow on gender remains because BIC USA permits women's ordination.

churches.assessment: HOPE Church (House of Prayer for Everyone) in Clarksville, MD is an ECO (Evangelical Covenant Order Presbyterian) congregation built around a house church model. Every member is integrated into a weekly house church gathering for dinner, fellowship, prayer, and Scripture — with corporate Sunday worship. ECO was formed in 2012 as a theologically conservative alternative to the PCUSA, affirming the Westminster Confession and biblical gender theology. This church's approach — Scripture-centered, prayer-saturated, community-integrated — reflects healthy early church patterns (Acts 2:42-46). For a man in the DC/Maryland area wanting deep discipleship, genuine community, and doctrinally sound Reformed theology, HOPE Church is a strong recommendation. The house church structure particularly builds the kind of accountable brotherhood that produces mature men.

churches.assessment: Kessler Park UMC is an explicitly and proudly LGBTQ+-affirming congregation in the Oak Cliff neighborhood of Dallas. The About page openly states the church is 'United Methodist in tradition, progressive in theology,' takes 'the Bible seriously, but not literally,' and is 'a proud member of the Reconciling Ministries Network.' The home page tagline ('A reconciling community of hope') and a prominent rainbow logo make the posture unambiguous. The church stayed in the post-2024 United Methodist Church through the disaffiliation window — the wing that formally removed restrictions on same-sex marriage and LGBTQ+ ordination at the 2024 General Conference. Pastoral team includes lead pastor Eric Folkerth (a self-described 'activist'), children's minister Kay Ash, and congregational care minister Ken Kelley. The directory user's tip of 'apostate, steer people away' is consistent with what the church openly publishes about itself: a progressive-mainline framework that has formally abandoned biblical authority on sexual ethics. Not recommended for men seeking a complementarian, inerrancy-affirming, Great-Commission-centered congregation.

churches.assessment: Lifepoint Church is the largest evangelical multi-campus operation in the Fredericksburg area, meeting at 1400 Central Park Blvd with three Sunday services. With six locations across Virginia and Kentucky, Lifepoint has infrastructure, resources, and a clear evangelical mission: "lead people far from God into a full life in Christ." Campus pastor Daniel leads a strong local team. However, Lifepoint exhibits the typical hallmarks of the large seeker-friendly non-denominational model: polished production, unclear doctrinal standards on gender/leadership, video preaching likely from a central teaching team, and life-group-driven community rather than classical discipleship. The mission is solid; the theological depth and complementarian backbone need verification. A man looking for a doctrinally rigorous, male-formation-focused church should visit with those specific questions in hand.

churches.assessment: Lutheran Church of Our Savior is the ELCA Lutheran congregation on Lejeune Boulevard — the main road between downtown Jacksonville NC and Camp Lejeune. The pastor, Mike Lang, is male, and the congregation likely contains many sincere Christians (including military families). But the denominational frame is the issue. ELCA's 2009 ChurchWide Assembly formally authorized the ordination of partnered same-sex clergy and the blessing of same-sex relationships; subsequent assemblies expanded that posture. ELCA has ordained women at all levels (including bishops) since 1970. The homepage greeting — "ALL are welcome" with open communion ("Holy Communion is available to all baptized Christians") — is consistent with the inclusive/welcoming identity ELCA has cultivated. This is institutional drift from biblical sexual ethics. Per MOOP rubric, ELCA congregations are flagged RED at the denominational level regardless of local pastor or local rhetorical conservatism. If Adam visited a Lutheran church near MCAS New River during V-22 training, this is the most visible Lutheran congregation on the Camp Lejeune corridor. Not recommended for MOOP-aligned theological convictions.

churches.assessment: Maranatha Baptist Church in Plains, Georgia is the small-town Baptist congregation where President Jimmy Carter taught Sunday school for nearly four decades — from 1981 until his health declined in 2019. The church drew international visitors who came specifically to hear Carter teach; he funeralized there in January 2025. Rev. Tony Lowden was Carter's personal pastor and the first Black lead pastor, succeeded by Rev. Ashley Guthas in 2024 — the church's first woman pastor (a divorced mother of two). In March 2025 under Guthas the church removed American flags from the sanctuary. Maranatha is independent / CBF-aligned (Cooperative Baptist Fellowship, formed 1991 by ex-SBC moderates over biblical-inerrancy and women-in-ministry questions). Carter himself publicly broke with the SBC over its 2000 BFM revision restricting women from senior pastor roles. Per MOOP rubric the female-senior-pastor + CBF-progressive denominational posture is RED on gender / leadership; included for situational awareness about the most famous lay-led Bible-teaching church in America under Carter.

churches.assessment: Marble Collegiate Church is one of America's most historically significant Reformed congregations, with roots back to 1628 and the current Marble building dedicated in 1854. Norman Vincent Peale served as pastor from 1932 to 1984, building a half-century legacy of positive-thinking preaching that profoundly shaped a young Donald Trump — whose family attended faithfully during his childhood and whose first wedding Peale officiated. Today Marble is led by Rev. Dr. Michael Bos and is openly LGBT-affirming, rejects biblical inerrancy in favor of historical-critical hermeneutics, performs same-sex weddings, and participates annually in NYC Pride. Dual-affiliated with the RCA and the UCC — both progressive mainlines, with the UCC being the most theologically progressive mainline in America. This is RED on the MOOP rubric; included for situational awareness about the formative church of a sitting president.

churches.assessment: Mennonite Christian Fellowship (MCF) — the namesake congregation of the small conservative Anabaptist denomination — is located in Atmore, Alabama. The MCF denomination originated in 1958 from early Amish revivalist groups in Holmes County, Ohio, and now numbers approximately 34 congregations and 1,500+ members nationwide. MCF practices plain dress, women's head covering, plural minister polity (bishop/minister/deacon), male-only ordination, and adheres to the Dordrecht Confession. The denomination publishes The Fellowship Contributor monthly. The Atmore congregation streams Sunday worship live on YouTube at 10:30 AM. Green rating reflects strong confessional, gender, leadership, and cultural integrity.

Horeb Church in Lexington, SC was South Carolina's largest United Methodist congregation before a dramatic 97% congregational vote on February 26, 2023 to leave the UMC, with formal GMC membership finalized in August 2023. Senior Pastor Jeff Kersey has led through this transition. The church runs two campuses (East traditional, West contemporary) with four services total each Sunday morning, and emphasizes making, maturing, and mobilizing disciples. Like all post-2022 GMC churches, the institutional commitment to orthodoxy (evidenced by the costly decision to leave UMC property and structure) is the strongest signal — these are congregations that paid a price to preserve biblical teaching on marriage and Christian doctrine. The GMC South Carolina Conference position on women as elders should be verified; otherwise this is a solidly orthodox Wesleyan option in the Columbia metro area.

Garfield and Lyndon B. Johnson, both Disciples. President Johnson occasionally attended during his presidency and his state funeral was held here on January 25, 1973. The church called The Rev. churches.assessment: Neon Reformed Presbyterian Church is an Orthodox Presbyterian Church congregation in Neon, Kentucky — deep in Letcher County in the Appalachian coal belt of southeastern Kentucky. This is a rare confessional Reformed presence in a region historically dominated by independent Old Regular Baptist, Free Will Baptist, and Pentecostal churches. The OPC's Presbytery of the Southeast covers southeastern Kentucky (rather than the Presbytery of Ohio). Rev. M. Jay Bennett serves as Pastor. For a man wanting strict-subscription Westminster Standards Presbyterianism in eastern Kentucky's mountains, Neon Reformed is functionally unique — a long-standing Appalachian OPC mission witness.

churches.gender_detail: Male-only ordained offices — elders and deacons (PCA enforces this at presbytery level)
churches.assessment: New City Fellowship is a downtown Fredericksburg gem hiding in plain sight. A PCA church at 200 Prince Edward St — walking distance from Moop's home area — with a clear expository preaching ministry, cross-cultural Great Commission mission, and the full doctrinal infrastructure of the Presbyterian Church in America behind it. The church website explicitly describes anticipating 'a word from the Lord' each Sunday through biblical preaching ('from every page of Scripture') — that's stated expository DNA, not just a marketing phrase. PCA means: Westminster Standards inerrancy, male-elder plurality with denominational accountability, complementarian polity enforced at the presbytery level, and Reformation soteriology. Rev. Robert M. Becker is a James River Presbytery-ordained pastor. The cross-cultural emphasis ('every nation, tribe, people, and language') ties directly to Matthew 28 and Acts 1:8 — healthy missional framing. The Sunday School model (9:30 AM) signals catechetical depth. If Moop is looking for a theologically robust, downtown, PCA congregation — this is the highest-confidence option found in Batch 4.

churches.assessment: Northwest Chapel is a Dublin, Ohio Grace Brethren congregation founded by — and still pastored by — Dr. Terry Hofecker since 1985, four decades and counting. He pulls double duty as Grace Theological Seminary faculty, was a volunteer Police Chaplain at the World Trade Center disaster site in fall 2001, and serves as Project Administrator for biblical archaeology excavations at Tel Gezer in Israel. That's the resume of a serious pastor-scholar. The Charis Fellowship — formerly Fellowship of Grace Brethren Churches, renamed in 2017 — holds dispensational evangelical theology with Anabaptist roots: complementarian, biblically-inerrantist, mission-oriented. Two Sunday services (9:15 and 11 AM), recovery ministry, full lifecycle ministry portfolio. For a Dublin or northwest-Columbus-area man wanting a doctrinally stable, scholar-led Grace Brethren church with multi-decade pastoral continuity, Northwest Chapel is one of the strongest options in central Ohio.

BF&M 1963 (no complementarian language) as doctrinal standard instead of BF&M 2000.
churches.assessment: Park Cities Baptist Church is a large Dallas megachurch (10,000 members, est. 1939) led by Dr. Jeff Warren since 2010. The church withdrew from the SBC in October 2024 specifically over the convention's push to restrict female pastors — a significant red flag for complementarian evaluation. Pastor Warren has publicly advocated for women in ministry, stating Jesus 'did not genderize the Great Commission.' The church affirms the 1963 Baptist Faith & Message (notably NOT the stricter 2000 version) and states men and women 'serve equally alongside each other.' Women serve on the Board of Trustees and chair standing committees. While the church maintains orthodox Christology, gospel-centered language, and active mission engagement, the explicit egalitarian trajectory places it in the RED category for gender/biblical design. The church remains affiliated with Texas Baptists (BGCT) and Dallas Baptist Association but has reduced denominational accountability after leaving the SBC. Not recommended for men seeking a church with complementarian convictions, but doctrinally sound on core gospel issues.

churches.assessment: Pohick Church is one of the oldest and most historically significant churches in Northern Virginia — originally built in 1774 and known as the parish of George Washington, George Mason, and other Virginia Founders. It is a landmark of American religious history. However, it remains affiliated with the Episcopal Church (TEC), which has undergone systematic theological abandonment since the 1970s — ordaining women as priests and bishops, affirming same-sex marriage, and ordaining LGBTQ+ clergy. The historic beauty of this church and its colonial American legacy are genuinely compelling, but the TEC institutional framework is doctrinally unreliable. Men seeking sound biblical preaching and complementarian theology should consider ACNA alternatives in Northern Virginia (such as The Falls Church Anglican or Truro Anglican), which left TEC precisely over these issues. Visit Pohick as a history lesson; find a sound church for your soul.

churches.assessment: Redeemer Bible Church is a recent and highly promising church plant out of Spotswood Baptist. It is solidly grounded in conservative evangelical theology, formally affirming the Baptist Faith & Message (2000). The church is led by a well-educated pastor, Victor (Vic) Carpenter, who holds a Ph.D. from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary. Their leadership structure includes a plurality of male elders, and they have dedicated ministries for men, women, and children. For anyone seeking a complementarian, SBC-affiliated church with a high view of Scripture and a commitment to discipleship and church planting, Redeemer Bible Church is an excellent option in the Spotsylvania area. MOOP-context note (Adam Johns, 2026): Adam attended both Redeemer Bible Spotsy and Stafford and characterizes the network as "splants" from his home church Spotswood Baptist — the new chain catered to Spotswood members who were "more Calvinist leaning" than Spotswood's SBC mainstream. The Calvinist/Reformed Baptist leaning is theologically substantive (more rigorous soteriology) but the church-network history is partly a tactical accommodation rather than a pure missional plant. Worth understanding as inheritor of Spotswood's baseline orthodoxy + Reformed-Baptist refinement.

score_notes.christology: Doctrinal statement explicitly affirms Trinity ("One Triune God eternally existent in three persons"), virgin birth, two natures in one Person of Christ, substitutionary atonement, bodily resurrection, ascension, and return in glory — fully Nicene/Chalcedonian.

score_notes.soteriology: Reformed-Baptist soteriology in the doctrinal essentials: total depravity ('man... has become separated from, and spiritually dead to God through Adam’s sin... possessing depraved human nature with no spark of divine life'), monergistic grace ('salvation is a free and permanent gift of God that cannot be secured or merited in part or in whole by any virtue or good work of man'), substitutionary atonement, perseverance ('salvation is inextricably bound to righteous living and good works and is the inevitable consequence (not the procuring cause) of the new life implanted by the Holy Spirit'). Sermon archive shows 6,321 messages across 58+ series including book studies of John, Galatians, Colossians, Ephesians, Habakkuk, Esther, Philemon, 1 Timothy, Hebrews, Psalms, and Sermon on the Mount — systematic exposition over years.

churches.assessment: Ridgecrest Baptist Church in Greenville is exactly the kind of church the directory wants to surface: 60-year-old (founded 1965) conservative SBC congregation, dual-aligned with the Southern Baptists of Texas Convention (the conservative split from BGCT, not the BGCT itself), explicitly adopting Baptist Faith & Message 2000, led by a plurality of male Staff Elders (Nick Dorsey, Joel Bench, Justin Milton) under the polity statement 'ruled by Jesus, led by the Elders, governed by the congregation' — the 9Marks elder-led-congregational pattern. The 'reformed-ish' descriptor the submitter used is well-earned: the doctrinal essentials affirm total depravity, monergistic grace, substitutionary atonement, and perseverance, even though the church does not formally subscribe to the 1689 London Baptist Confession or claim a Founders Ministry affiliation on its public site. Preaching is explicitly verse-by-verse expository, with a sermon archive of 6,321 messages spanning systematic book studies (John, Galatians, Colossians, Ephesians, Habakkuk, Esther, Philemon, 1 Timothy, Hebrews, Psalms, Sermon on the Mount). The 'RidgeMen' men's ministry is dedicated and pastor-led. The local missions arm 'For the City' (launched 2017) and a Spanish-language plant from 1981 demonstrate Great Commission seriousness. churches.assessment: River Oak Church is a strong SBC option for Hampton Roads-area men. The church plants out of South Norfolk Baptist Church (1998 land purchase, 1999 first service at Oscar F. Smith High School, 2000 formal constitution, 2007 facility opening on Great Bridge Blvd), and adopts the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 verbatim. The doctrinal statement hits every conservative-evangelical mark: triune God, full deity and exclusivity of Christ, inerrant Scripture as 'totally true and trustworthy...without any mixture of error,' salvation by grace through faith alone, believer's baptism by immersion, complementarian marriage and pastoral office ('the office of pastor is limited to men'), and explicit opposition to homosexuality and sexual immorality. Governance is 'Council-Led, Congregational' — a hybrid plural-elder + congregational-vote model where the three Co-Lead Pastors (Hammen, Waldrop, LaRussa, all called 2024) plus four elected male lay councilors function as elders/overseers/pastors and the congregation votes on budgets, officer elections, constitutional amendments, and pastoral calls. Preaching is expository (current series through Titus and Mark). Dedicated Men's Ministry with Men's Groups and the ManCake breakfast confirms intentional men's discipleship. No DEI/CRT or affirming language found on the public pages. Green across all ten dimensions.

Consider Missouri Synod or Wisconsin Synod Lutheran alternatives in the area.

churches.assessment: Rivermont Evangelical Presbyterian Church is one of Lynchburg's most theologically distinguished congregations. Founded in 1881 — over 140 years of ministry in the same Lynchburg neighborhood — Rivermont operates under the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms within the EPC (Evangelical Presbyterian Church). Dr. David Weber's preaching is highly regarded by long-time members. The church's membership in the New River Presbytery provides genuine external accountability, confessional standards, and doctrinal oversight absent in independent churches. For a man wanting Reformed theology, historic confessional Christianity, and a church with deep Lynchburg roots and community presence, Rivermont EPC is a top-tier choice. The Campus Outreach ministry on staff signals a heart for the next generation.

For men committed to biblical male-only eldership/pastoral leadership, this is a disqualifying red flag. Rock Church has genuine gospel impact and community roots, but the gender/leadership structure places it outside clear biblical complementarianism.

churches.assessment: Second Baptist Church (West End) is a historically important Richmond Black congregation with roots stretching over 185 years. Rev. Dr. James Henry Harris is a serious scholar — Distinguished Professor of Homiletics at Virginia Union University and a published theologian. The problem: Rev. Harris is an academic whose theological framework is aligned with Black liberation theology, a school of thought that subordinates Scripture to the experience of racial oppression and reinterprets the Gospel through social and political liberation categories. This is not a Reformed or evangelical framework — it places experience and culture above Scripture's authority. For men seeking a doctrinally sound, Great Commission-focused church, Second Baptist (West End) is not the right fit. The historical legacy is real and deserves respect; the current theological direction is not.

churches.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (Old Site) is one of Fredericksburg's most historically significant congregations — founded in 1854 from a congregation dating to the early 1800s, serving the African American community through slavery, the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the Civil Rights era. Notable members include John Washington (whose escape from slavery inspired a Trail to Freedom) and Rev. Lawrence A. Davies (pastor and mayor of Fredericksburg). The church's commitment to community (free Wednesday breakfast with Micah Ecumenical Ministries, active youth ministry) reflects genuine love. The honest theological concern is the public framing: 'no barriers to God's grace, no walls of exclusion' and 'inclusive embrace' language combined with minimal gospel-clarity and strong social-service identity suggests the congregation may have drifted toward social gospel territory where the transforming work of Christ is framed primarily in terms of social healing rather than personal salvation and sanctification. This is a pattern in mainline-influenced progressive Baptist churches. Moop should visit and listen to the sermons directly before drawing conclusions.

churches.assessment: Sparta RPC is a historic Covenanter congregation in Southern Illinois — Sparta has been an RPCNA outpost since the 19th century, when Covenanter Scots-Irish settlers planted churches across the rural Midwest. Holds Westminster Confession with strict confessional subscription, practices exclusive psalmody and a cappella worship (no instruments), maintains twice-Sunday services. Male-only ordination, deeply complementarian, no cultural drift. The exclusive psalmody and a cappella worship will be a major adjustment for those not raised in this tradition, but Sparta represents one of the oldest unbroken confessional Reformed witnesses in the rural Midwest. Illinois has very few RPCNA congregations; Sparta is a meaningful historic anchor.

churches.assessment: Sen. Edmund S. Muskie (D-ME) — U.S. Senator 1959-1980, Governor of Maine 1955-1959 (the state's first Roman Catholic governor), Secretary of State 1980-1981 under President Carter, and 1968 Democratic vice-presidential nominee — was born March 28, 1914 in Rumford, Maine to Polish immigrant parents Stephen Marciszewski (anglicized to Muskie 1914) and Josephine née Czarnecka. Muskie's first language was Polish; he spoke only Polish until age 4. St. Athanasius Church — established 1895 on Maine Avenue, sanctuary rebuilt 1928 — was the primary Roman Catholic parish serving Rumford's Polish and Eastern European immigrant Catholic community during Muskie's childhood. While Wikipedia's Muskie biography directly confirms his Roman Catholic identity ("the state's first Roman Catholic governor") and his Polish-Rumford upbringing without explicitly naming the parish, St. Athanasius's historic role as the Rumford Polish Catholic parish makes it the logical family parish; the Franco American Digital Archives Edmund S. Muskie Oral History Collection contains an interview specifically referencing St. Athanasius and St. John Parish Rumford in connection with Muskie. Currently merged into the Parish of the Holy Savior under Fr. Aaron Damboise; building remains at 126 Maine Avenue.

score_notes.gender: Roman Catholic Church maintains male-only ordained priesthood — women cannot be priests. score_notes.soteriology: Roman Catholic soteriology — Council of Trent (1547) anathematized justification by faith alone; salvation is faith + works + sacraments (Eucharist, confession, penance, purgatory, indulgences). This is a fundamental break with the Reformation gospel and therefore with the MOOP rubric's sola fide requirement. Orthodox Trinitarian Christology and male-only priests are preserved, but the gospel itself is modified.

score_notes.mens_discipleship: Knights of Columbus or other men's organizations are standard in active Catholic parishes like St. Mary's.
score_notes.denominational: Excellent accountability: Diocese of Arlington is conservative and supervised; full apostolic succession and diocesan governance.

churches.gender_detail: Male-only priesthood (Catholic doctrine) but no explicit biblical patriarchal household framework
churches.assessment: Saint Mary's is a large, active Catholic parish in Fredericksburg under the conservative Diocese of Arlington. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane — essentially the area dean — indicating a significant, well-resourced congregation. Trinitarian orthodoxy is rock-solid; male-only priesthood is firmly complementarian; accountability structure is hierarchical and thorough. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the theological divergence is real: Catholic soteriology adds sacraments, merit, and ecclesial mediation to faith; Scripture sits alongside Tradition rather than above it. These are not minor differences — they were the substance of the Reformation. That said, for a man interested in robust liturgy, deep historical tradition, strong pro-life stance, and conservative moral theology, the Diocese of Arlington Catholic experience is among the best available. Not the right fit for a faith-alone evangelical, but should be evaluated on its own terms.

As one of America's oldest churches (1734), it separated from The Episcopal Church over homosexuality and women's ordination, fought a legal battle that cost them their historic building, and re-planted as a faithful Anglican congregation. They now worship at an office building — having chosen doctrinal integrity over real estate. Rector Sam Ferguson leads a congregation with deep roots in biblical Anglicanism, liturgical worship rooted in Scripture, and a legacy of sending. ACNA accountability, male-only priesthood, complementarian household vision. For a man who values covenantal worship, historic liturgy, and a congregation that has paid a price for orthodoxy — this is worth serious consideration.

Worth a visit; go in knowing you're in moderate Baptist territory, not SBC.

churches.assessment: Third Baptist Church of San Francisco is the oldest African-American Baptist congregation west of the Rockies (founded 1852). For nearly half a century — 1976 to 2025 — it was pastored by Rev. Amos C. Brown, a civil-rights leader and close advisor to Kamala Harris. Brown gave the convention prayer at the 2024 DNC. Harris has been a member for more than 20 years and worked for Brown's campaign for San Francisco supervisor in 2000; he was reportedly among the first people she called when Joe Biden suspended his 2024 campaign and she became the presumptive Democratic nominee. Rev. Devon Jerome Crawford succeeded Brown on July 1, 2025. Theologically the congregation operates in the progressive Black social-gospel tradition with heavy reparations and racial-justice framing; ABC-USA affiliation places it on the affirming end of Baptist polity. Per MOOP rubric this is RED; included for situational awareness about the home church of a recent Democratic nominee for President.

score_notes.scripture: Strong inerrancy affirmation: Bible has 'truth, without any mixture of error, for its matter' and 'all Scripture is totally true and trustworthy.' Clear complementarian theology.

score_notes.mission: Mission: 'helping people far from God know Christ through global, domestic, and local impact.' Global Mission Coordinator on staff. Community ministries. College ministry. Spanish-language outreach. Great Commission-oriented.

churches.gender_detail: COMPLEMENTARIAN. All-male elder board (7 elders). All pastoral/minister titles held by men. churches.assessment: Travis Avenue Baptist Church is a historic SBC church in Fort Worth led by Lead Teaching Pastor Benjamin Bolin with a 7-member all-male elder board. This is one of the strongest doctrinal profiles in the directory: explicit inerrancy affirmation ('truth, without any mixture of error'), comprehensive salvation theology (regeneration, justification, sanctification, glorification), clear complementarian position in beliefs statement (husband as head, wife submitting graciously), and elder-led governance. The church offers three concurrent worship styles (choir-led, band-led, Spanish) and has strong Great Commission mission language. The main gap is the lack of a dedicated men's ministry despite having women's ministry programs — an oversight for a church with otherwise excellent theological infrastructure. SBC-affiliated with strong denominational accountability. Recommended for evaluation — visit to verify preaching quality and cultural alignment in person.

churches.assessment: President Warren G. Harding joined the Free Baptist Church in Marion on May 6, 1883, served as a trustee for 25 years and as a deacon, and remained a member until his death in 1923. The Free Baptist Church merged with the First Baptist Church via a joint worship service on September 24, 1911, and was renamed Trinity Baptist Church in April 1912. The congregation that today carries Harding's historical pew has, in the contemporary era, embraced a robust 1689 London Baptist Confession Reformed Baptist confessional identity under Pastor Daniel McCoy (DTS / Master's Seminary), with explicit 9Marks and Founders Ministries affiliation. Worth noting: Harding personally was a theologically liberal Baptist (per Patheos historical assessment), so the present-day Trinity Baptist is more confessionally robust than the congregation Harding inhabited.

churches.assessment: The Trinity Church is Mark Driscoll's post-Mars Hill comeback church in Scottsdale, AZ. Theologically, Driscoll is one of the strongest Reformed voices in America — his Christology, soteriology, complementarian gender theology, and expository preaching are excellent. churches.assessment: Trinity United Methodist Church is the small-town Kansas Methodist church where Bob Dole grew up — his parents sent the Dole children "most Sundays" per multiple biographies, and the town of Russell held its public memorial farewell to Dole at this church when he died in 2021. The church remains active in the United Methodist Connection — affiliated with the Great Plains Conference. Following the 2019-2023 disaffiliation window, those UMC churches that remained (including Trinity Russell) are now part of a denomination that at General Conference 2024 removed restrictions on ordination of openly gay clergy and same-sex weddings. This places UMC churches at red on MOOP's rubric across gender, cultural, and denominational dimensions — irrespective of any individual rural congregation's personal practice. The local Trinity Russell congregation is small (rural Kansas town of c.4,000), traditional in worship style, and historically significant as Bob Dole's home church.

churches.assessment: Vienna Presbyterian Church is a historic PCUSA congregation in Vienna, VA. The PCUSA (Presbyterian Church USA) is the mainline Presbyterian denomination that voted in 2015 to approve same-sex marriage and has long ordained women as elders and pastors. This represents a fundamental departure from the Westminster Confession of Faith, the Reformed theological tradition, and biblical authority on sexuality. Individual PCUSA congregations vary — some maintain more conservative pastoral leadership despite the denomination's drift. However, the denominational framework means that membership contributions flow toward an institution that actively promotes positions contrary to biblical sexuality and clear scriptural authority. For men wanting Reformed theology with denominational integrity, the PCA (Presbyterian Church in America), the OPC (Orthodox Presbyterian Church), or ECO are the sound alternatives. Vienna has multiple PCA and ACNA options that hold the confessional line.

churches.assessment: Vineville Baptist Church (Macon GA) is a moderate-Baptist congregation dual-aligned with the Georgia Baptist Mission Board (SBC) and the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship of Georgia. Senior Pastor Rev. Greg Pope is male, but two of the four pastoral-track positions on the church's staff page are filled by ordained women bearing the title 'Rev.': Rev. Angela Blizzard (Minister of Music, on staff since 2007) and Rev. Leigh Halverson (Minister of Family Life and Education). The church's children's ministry uses CBF curriculum. While the staff use 'Minister' rather than 'Pastor' in formal titling, the practice of ordaining women to staff ministry sits in direct tension with BF&M 2000 Article VI as the SBC currently interprets it.

The church self-describes with three pillars — 'Bible-believing, Jesus-teaching, and people-loving' — which is clean evangelical language. FaithStreet confirms SBC affiliation, giving a solid denominational foundation on inerrancy, complementarianism, and soteriology. 'Pastor Patrick' is Moop's friend, which is the relational glue that makes this worth visiting. BGAV directory lists a different pastor name (Rev. John Shutlock), which may reflect an outdated directory or a recent pastoral transition to Pastor Patrick. The traditional service format and rural context suggest a conservative, no-frills congregation. No dedicated men's ministry found, but Moop's existing relationship makes this a personal as much as a theological connection.

churches.assessment: Washington Community Fellowship is a long-standing evangelical congregation in NE Washington, DC (Capitol Hill area) with Mennonite/Anabaptist roots, describing itself as 'Christ-centered' and called to personal transformation, authentic community, and social impact. The Anabaptist tradition (Mennonite, Brethren) is one of the historic Reformation streams, historically emphasizing discipleship, community, peacemaking, and radical following of Jesus. Strengths: genuine community emphasis, NE DC neighborhood engagement, ecumenical but Christ-centered orientation. Cautions: Anabaptist traditions vary widely on Scripture's authority and gender roles; many Mennonite-affiliated churches have moved toward egalitarian and progressive positions. Review their current statement of faith, pastoral authority structure, and specific positions on gender and sexuality. A community-focused church with historic roots — warrants direct investigation.

churches.assessment: West End Presbyterian is a PCA congregation in Richmond's West End — and PCA means a lot here. The Presbyterian Church in America is one of the most theologically rigorous denominations in America: inerrancy of Scripture, Westminster Confession of Faith, male-only elders, faith-alone soteriology, and complementarian theology are all baked into the PCA constitution. Rev. Steven Shelby leads a church with a clearly stated mission: 'make followers of Jesus who bring the Gospel to bear on every facet of life and culture.' The staff includes associate pastors for youth and neighborhood outreach, suggesting a full-orbed ministry. For any man seeking a doctrinally robust, Gospel-centered, Word-saturated church home in Richmond, West End Presbyterian belongs at the top of the list.

churches.assessment: Sen. John H. Glenn Jr. (D-OH), Marine fighter pilot, first American to orbit Earth (Friendship 7, 1962), four-term U.S. Senator (1974-1999), and at age 77 the oldest astronaut in spaceflight (STS-95, 1998), was raised in this New Concord congregation by his parents John Herschel and Clara Glenn. Glenn's mother was the first female Ruling Elder ordained at Westminster; his father was also a Ruling Elder. Glenn himself was a lifelong Presbyterian Ruling Elder. He and his wife Annie alternated between Westminster (John's family) and College Drive Presbyterian (Annie's family) during their hometown visits. In Washington he attended National Presbyterian Church and served on its Session. The church is currently a PC(USA) mainline congregation under Rev. Ellen Thomas, reflecting denominational shifts that occurred decades after Glenn's formation.

churches.assessment: Williamsburg Community Chapel has served the Williamsburg community as an interdenominational evangelical congregation for many years. The church's constitutional foundation — 'interdenominational church wherein all of those who love Jesus Christ and desire to serve Him may join in one common effort' — reflects a broad evangelical unity emphasis.
